output.reason: A 71-year-old with hip pain and inability to bear weight after a fall this morning needs immediate emergency imaging and orthopedic assessment for probable hip fracture, which messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. A fall with severe hip pain and inability to put weight on that leg strongly suggests a hip fracture needing urgent X-rays and orthopedic care. Do not walk on that leg or drive yourself — have someone take you, or call 911 if no one can help, or if you feel faint, short of breath, or the leg becomes numb, cold or pale.
differential: Femoral neck or intertrochanteric hip fracture
Hip dislocation or pubic ramus/pelvic fracture

redFlags.quote: I can't put any weight on that leg

citations.claim: Hip/groin pain with inability to bear weight after a ground-level fall in an elderly patient is the classic hip fracture presentation.
citations.limitation: Compiled synthesis; fracture not confirmed without imaging.

citations.claim: Occult fractures occur with normal radiographs in patients unable to bear weight, so imaging pathways matter.
citations.limitation: Applies to imaging strategy, not routing per se.
